title: Isolation and Cultivation of Primary Respiratory Epithelial Cells
author: Golec, Pranke, et al.

steps.title: Set up sterile workspace and equipment
steps.instruction: Perform all work in a sterile biosafety cabinet while wearing required PPE; allocate a dedicated 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for primary cultures; prepare collagen‑coated filters and flasks, and pre‑make all media and buffers.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic‑supplemented culture medium
steps.instruction: Add sterile antibiotic liquids (from hospital pharmacy) or dissolve antibiotic powders, filter‑sterilize, and mix into the basal culture medium as described for CF patients; adjust with any additional antibiotics based on the subject’s antibiogram.

steps.title: Collect nasal epithelial cells by brushing
steps.instruction: Obtain nasal epithelial cells using a sterile brush after local anesthesia; keep samples on ice or at room temperature (18‑23 °C) and add antibiotics if required before transport.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two 15 mL tubes with 2.5 mL room‑temperature PBS (or FertiCult); label with subject ID and date; record genotype and known antibiotic resistance on the data sheet.
Assemble four sterile cotton meshes (two 5 cm, two 10 cm) and soak in 5 % xylocaine with naphazoline; squeeze excess liquid and roll the end to be inserted first.
Apply the first set of 5 cm meshes to each nostril with Politzer tweezers, leave 5 min, then remove.
Apply the second set of 10 cm meshes, leave at least 10 min, then remove; ask the subject to blow the nose.
Wet the nasal brush in sterile PBS (or FertiCult) in a 15 mL tube.

Insert the brush horizontally between the inferior and middle turbinate, rotate/linearly 5‑10 times in the lower middle third of the inferior turbinate; repeat for each nostril (minimum one brush per nostril, ideally two).
Place the brush back into the labeled tube, shake vigorously for 15 s, cut the wire if needed so the brush fits, seal the tube and keep on ice (or at 18‑23 °C if in FertiCult) for transport.
If using FertiCult tubes for shipping, add 0.1 mL antibiotic solution to each tube under sterile conditions.

steps.title: Process nasal brush sample before expansion
steps.instruction: Recover cells from the brush, enzymatically dissociate, and seed into collagen‑coated flasks (Passage 0).

substeps.instruction: Use the brush sheath to scrape cells into the tube; discard the brush.
Centrifuge tube at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Add 0.5 mL Trypsin, resuspend, incubate 5‑7 min at 37 °C.
Add 1 mL amplification medium to stop trypsin, combine contents of both tubes, mix gently.
Centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL amplification medium.
Distribute cell suspension into collagen‑coated flasks: 10 mL medium for a 75 cm² flask or 5 mL for a 25 cm² flask (defines Passage 0).
Place flasks in the 37 °C incubator; check for attachment after 12‑24 h.

steps.title: Isolate cells from lung explant (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare lung bronchial tissue, wash, and incubate with Pronase overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transport lung explant on wet ice in PBS or culture medium; process within 24 h.
Place whole explant with transport medium into a 10 cm sterile Petri dish.
Using a sterile scalpel, discard necrotic bronchial portions and transfer cleaned bronchial pieces to an empty 50 mL tube.
Wash bronchial pieces twice with 25 mL PBS‑DTT‑FTVC (room temperature 18‑23 °C), shaking 30 s each, aspirating after each wash.
Rinse twice with 25 mL PBS‑FTVC to remove DTT.
Add 14 mL pre‑warmed DMEM/F12‑FTVC to the tube to keep tissue moist.
Add 4 mL Pronase to the tube (now 36 mL DMEM/F12‑FTVC), aspirate the 14 mL medium, and return bronchial pieces to the Pronase solution.
Incubate overnight (12 h optimal, minimum 4 h) at 4 °C on a rotator set to 10‑20 rpm.

steps.title: Isolate cells from lung explant (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Recover, neutralize, and seed epithelial cells from the explant after Pronase digestion.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant, leaving 20 mL; pass this through a 100 µm sterile stainless‑steel strainer into a clean 50 mL tube.
Add 20 mL DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC to neutralize Pronase; mix and vortex 2 min.
Transfer the content to a 15 cm Petri dish; bisect the bronchial piece and scrape the lumen side with a sterile scalpel to release cells.
Rinse the bronchial piece twice with DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC, collecting the rinse into the 50 mL tube via the strainer; rinse the dish once more and collect.
Centrifuge the combined cell suspension at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C (distribute into two 50 mL tubes if volume large).
Aspirate supernatant and add 1‑5 mL Trypsin (volume based on pellet size); resuspend gently and incubate 7 min at 37 °C.
Add up to 5 mL DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC to stop trypsin, mix gently.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 2‑5 mL amplification medium, count cells (15 µL on counting chamber).
Seed 500 000 cells per 75 cm² flask with 10 mL amplification medium; place flasks in the 37 °C incubator (defines Passage 0).

steps.title: Isolate cells from polyp tissue (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Wash polyp tissue, treat with Pronase, and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Thaw Pronase and prepare dissociation media in advance.
Aspirate transport medium from the 50 mL tube (avoid aspirating small polyps).
Place the polyp into an empty 50 mL Falcon tube.
Wash twice with 25 mL PBS‑DTT, shaking 1 min each, aspirating after each wash.
Rinse twice with 25 mL PBS‑FTVC, shaking 1 min each, aspirating after each rinse.
Add 14 mL DMEM/F12‑FTVC to the tube to keep the polyp moist.
Add 4 mL Pronase to the tube (now 36 mL DMEM/F12‑FTVC), aspirate the 14 mL medium, and return the polyp to the Pronase solution.
Incubate overnight (minimum 12 h) at 4 °C on a rotator set to 10‑20 rpm; note the start time.

steps.title: Isolate cells from polyp tissue (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Neutralize Pronase, collect cells, and seed into flasks.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant, leaving 20 mL; add 20 mL DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC to neutralize Pronase; mix and vortex 2 min.
Pass the polyp and medium through a sterile 100 µm stainless‑steel strainer into a 15 cm Petri dish (keep the original tube).
Rinse the polyp twice with 5 mL DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC using a pipette stream; collect rinses in the original tube via the strainer; rinse the dish again and collect.
Centrifuge the combined cell suspension at 1 500 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant and add 1‑2 mL Trypsin (2 mL for larger pellets); resuspend and incubate 7 min at 37 °C.
Add 5 mL DMEM/F12‑FBS20 %‑FTVC, mix gently.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in amplification medium (1‑4 mL depending on size), count cells (15 µL on counting chamber).
Seed 500 000 cells per 75 cm² flask with 10 mL amplification medium; incubate at 37 °C (Passage 0).

steps.title: Expand primary epithelial cells
steps.instruction: Maintain cultures, change medium, monitor growth, and handle contamination; freeze a portion after first passage.

substeps.instruction: Day after seeding (only this day): aspirate medium from each flask, rinse with 10 mL PBS‑FTVC, aspirate, then add fresh amplification medium (10 mL for T75, 5 mL for T25).
Inspect cells daily for attachment, epithelial morphology, confluence, and medium clarity.
Change medium every 48‑72 h: aspirate old medium and add fresh amplification medium (10 mL for T75, 5 mL for T25).

If medium becomes cloudy, sample it for microbiology, rinse cells with 10 mL adapted PBS‑FTVC, add amplification medium containing patient‑specific antibiotics (or Ciprofloxacin if unknown), and notify the lab manager.
Freeze a portion of expanded cells after the first passage (0.5‑1 × 10⁶ cells per cryovial); if cell numbers are low, freeze at Passage 1 (P1).
General guidelines: do not seed directly onto filters; keep WT and CF cultures on separate labeled shelves; change medium in any flask suspected of contamination at the end of handling.

steps.title: Seed expanded cells onto collagen‑coated filters
steps.instruction: Detach cells, count, calculate required cell number per filter, and seed onto pre‑coated filters.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑coat filters with collagen as described in Materials.
Aspirate medium from a 75 cm² flask, add 10 mL PBS, aspirate, then add 2 mL Trypsin; incubate 7 min at 37 °C.
Tap the flask to aid detachment; add 10 mL amplification medium to stop trypsin, rinse vigorously to collect cells.
If cells remain attached, repeat trypsinization with an additional 2 mL Trypsin for ≤5 min.
Transfer cell suspension to a 50 mL tube, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 3‑5 mL amplification medium (volume based on pellet size).
Take 15 µL of suspension, place on a counting chamber (Malassez or equivalent), count cells in 10 small squares, and calculate total cell number (cells = count × 10⁴ × suspension volume in mL).
Determine number of filters feasible (total cells ÷ cells per filter; 330‑350 000 cells per 0.33 cm² filter).
Add calculated cell suspension to the apical side of each filter; adjust apical volume to 300 µL (add amplification medium if less).
Add 900 µL amplification medium to the basal compartment.

steps.title: Maintain filters before air‑liquid interface
steps.instruction: Perform routine medium changes on apical and basal sides before establishing ALI.

substeps.instruction: Do not remove apical medium until day 2‑3; if left longer (up to 5 days) replace with fresh 300 µL amplification medium.
Change basal medium every 48‑72 h: aspirate old basal medium and add 900 µL fresh ALI medium.
If medium appears cloudy, send sample for microbiology, rinse apical side with 300 µL adapted PBS‑FTVC, and add fresh 300 µL amplification medium containing appropriate antibiotics.
Use separate pipette tips for apical and basal manipulations to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Initiate air‑liquid interface culture
steps.instruction: Remove apical medium and maintain cells at ALI; change basal medium regularly.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate and discard all apical medium; from now on the apical side remains medium‑free.
Aspirate and discard basal medium, then add 900 µL fresh ALI medium to the basal compartment.
Replace basal medium every 48‑72 h thereafter.
Allow differentiation for 15‑30 days; monitor for cilia formation and epithelial maturation.
If ALI medium leaks onto the apical side (usually ~7 days), suspect poor filter quality.

steps.title: Measure transepithelial electrical resistance
steps.instruction: Use an EVOM2 volt/ohm meter to assess monolayer integrity on filters.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the EVOM2 and sterilize both electrodes by submerging in 70 % ethanol for several seconds; air‑dry.
Connect electrodes to the meter, set function to Ohms, mode to R, and range to 20 kΩ.
Measure blank resistance (R_blank) by placing the short electrode in the apical compartment (filled with sterile saline if needed) and the long electrode in the basal compartment; record value.
Measure sample resistance (R_sample) in the same way; perform at least duplicate measurements quickly to minimize temperature effects.
Calculate TEER: (R_sample − R_blank) × 0.33 cm² (membrane area).
If measuring on ALI cultures, add ~100 µL sterile physiological saline to the apical side to allow electrode contact, then remove after measurement.

steps.title: Freeze cultured cells for biobanking
steps.instruction: Cryopreserve cells at P0‑P2 using controlled‑rate freezing and store in liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Prepare freezing medium as described in Materials.
Label cryovials with subject ID, site ID, cell type, passage number, date, and operator initials.
Select a confluent 75 cm² flask (80‑90 % confluence, P0‑P2).
Aspirate medium, add 10 mL PBS, then aspirate PBS to remove residual medium.
Add 2 mL Trypsin, incubate 7 min at 37 °C; tap flask to detach cells.
Neutralize trypsin with 10 mL amplification medium, rinse the surface, and repeat detachment steps to maximize yield.
Collect cell suspension in a 50 mL tube, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in enough regular medium to obtain a count, then count cells.
Resuspend 1‑2 × 10⁶ cells per 1 mL freezing medium; aliquot into labeled cryovials.
Place cryovials in a Mr. Frosty container and store at −80 °C overnight.
Transfer vials the next day to a liquid‑nitrogen storage tank for long‑term preservation.

steps.title: Defrost frozen cells
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw cryovials, recover cells, and re‑seed into culture flasks.

substeps.instruction: Warm a water bath to 37 °C; pre‑warm amplification medium to 37 °C.
Remove cryovial from liquid nitrogen, place in the water bath for up to 2 min (do not submerge the vial).
Wipe the vial label with alcohol to avoid loss of information.
Transfer thawed cells to an empty 15 mL tube using a 1 mL pipette.
Add 1 mL warm amplification medium drop‑wise, wait 1 min; repeat with another 1 mL, wait another minute.
Add 10 mL amplification medium to bring volume to 12 mL, then centrifuge 2 min at 230 × g.
Aspirate supernatant, note the original frozen cell number, and resuspend pellet in amplification medium to achieve ≥1 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
Seed cells into flasks: up to 2 × 10⁶ cells in 10 mL for a 75 cm² flask, or up to 4 × 10⁶ cells in 15 mL for a 150 cm² flask.
Place flasks in the 37 °C incubator and monitor expansion over the next 2‑3 days.

description: This protocol presents all the necessary information for conducting successful cell culture without co-culture of the feeder cells (fibroblasts). Non-proliferating, yet metabolically active fibroblasts can be used to boost cultures that originate from very low starting cell inoculum. Feeder cells support improved attachment of the desired cells and secrete growth factors and nutrients into the culture medium. The mitotic arrest of the feeder cells is often achieved by either Mitomycin C treatment or gamma-ray irradiation. Both of these methods confer a hazardous risk to the operator. Mitomycin C is regarded as a probable human carcinogen and the availability of gamma irradiation sources is very limited. Therefore, we have decided to omit the use of the feeder cells in this protocol. We acknowledge the potential beneficial effects of the co-culture and do not exclude the possibility of other laboratories conducting these cultures. We have included procedures for 1) nasal brushing, and handling of polyp and lung explant samples; and 2) freezing/defrosting for biobanking of samples involved in clinical trials. Please note, that despite strict adherence to the following protocol, a 100% success rate of the cell culture cannot be guaranteed, particularly for samples obtained by nasal brushing. The quality and quantity of the brushed material, variability in patients’ characteristics (including concomitant infections), as well as the specific CF mutation, can all play a crucial role in obtaining a good quality culture. Limitations of this protocol may include variation from laboratory to laboratory in terms of the use of antibiotics. This protocol represents the authors’ preferred methods of choice and any variation in local site procedure should be discussed on a case-by-case basis.
